newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL-CANADIENS BEAT FLAMES ON THREE SHORT-HANDED GOALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-CANADIENS BEAT FLAMES ON THREE SHORT-HANDED GOALS.

text.p: The Montreal Canadiens outplayed the Calgary Flames with fewer skaters on the ice on Wednesday, coming up with three short-handed goals in a 4-2 victory.
Scott Thornton, Martin Rucinsky and Marc Bureau all scored for Montreal while Calgary was on the powerplay, and Pat Jablonksi made 42 saves as the Canadiens triumphed despite being outshot 44-27.
"Jablonski was unbelievable," said Calgary's Theo Fleury. "When you get 44 shots on goal you should be able to score at least four or five. Jablonksi stole two points from us."
The three short-handed goals tied a team record set in 1948 in a 7-4 win over the Chicago Blackhawks.
Thornton, who opened the scoring with a short-handed tally 8:35 into the game, was sent to the penalty box on a double high-sticking minor with score tied 2-2 in the second period.

Instead of Calgary making the most of its golden opportunity, Montreal snapped the tie at 4:28 when Rucinsky breezed past Cory Stillman, cut to the front of the Flames goal and beat Rick Tabaracci through the pads.

With Thornton still in the box, Montreal made it 4-2 just over three minutes later. Bureau raced through the neutral zone and beat rookie Jonas Hoglund down the right wing before slipping a backhand past an outstretched Tabaracci.
"Penalty killing turned the game around for us and we took some bad penalties out there, especially in the third period," said Montreal coach Mario Tremblay.
Jablonski, making his first start of the season, surrendered first-period goals to Dave Gagner and Hoglund. But he turned back all 30 shots he faced over the final two periods.
"Jablonski was outstanding," said Tremblay. "I've seen some great goaltending in my career but that was about the best."
In New York, Alexei Kovalev had a hat trick and Niklas Sundstrom scored twice as the struggling Rangers erupted offensively for an 8-1 thumping of the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Mike Richter made 29 saves in goal for New York as the Rangers picked up their second successive victory after going winless in their first five games.
Mark Messier and Wayne Gretzky each contributed two assists for the Rangers, who peppered the Pittsburgh goal with 48 shots on net.
Kovalev opened the scoring 7:16 into the game when he took a pass from Messier and snapped a shot past Pittsburgh goaltender Tom Barrasso.

After New York increased its lead to 4-1 in the second on rookie Daniel Goneau's third goal in as many games, Brian Leetch found a streaking Kovalev, who managed to sweep a backhand between Barrasso's pads while falling down.
Barrasso was replaced by Ken Wregget, who surrendered three more goals, including Kovalev's third of the night at 9:02 of the third to make it 7-1.
In San Jose, Jeff Friesen's second goal of the game with 6:37 left in the third period lifted the Sharks to a 3-3 tie with the Florida Panthers.
Michal Sykora and Friesen scored in the first, staking San Jose to a 2-0 lead as Florida allowed two goals in a period for the first time this season.
Florida answered with a three-goal third on tallies by Gord Murphy, Johan Garpenlov and Dave Lowry, who put the Panthers in front with 7:30 left in regulation.
Despite blowing the 3-2 lead less than a minute later, the Panthers remained one of two unbeaten teams in the NHL with a 3-0-2 record.
In Anaheim, Pat Falloon scored with 7:53 remaining to cap a three-goal rally as the Philadelphia Flyers snapped a three-game losing streak with a 4-3 win over the Mighty Ducks.
Teemu Selanne scored a powerplay goal 2:18 into the second period to give the Ducks a 3-1 lead, but the Flyers scored the final three goals.
Ron Hextall settled down after a skaky start, finishing with 24 saves for Philadelphia.
John Druce and Mikael Reneberg tied the game for the Flyers, each picking up his first goal of the season, before Druce set up Falloon's game winner.
